Thanks again for taking time last week. As discussed, I wanted to kick off a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so we have clear owners, milestones, and a realistic close timeline for your evaluation. Goal: get a production-safe prototype running against a representative workload and agree on success criteria by the end of Q3 (target close: 2026-09-30).

- Customer lead: Sam Gray (Helix) — owns dataset access and internal stakeholder sign-off
- PM / lines of business: Joanna Lee (Helix) — owns business acceptance criteria
- Redwood AE: Rishi Malhotra — program lead and commercial questions
- Redwood SE: Camila Reyes — technical onboarding, demos, and performance tuning
- Redwood ML Eng: Diego Fernandez — model/configuration recommendations and eval plan

Initial asks (can we confirm by EOD Wed?):
1) Your preferred evaluation window (2–4 weeks typical) and any blackout dates
2) Access to a representative sample dataset (S3 link or shared Drive) or a data spec
3) Primary success metrics (latency P95, token cost, QA pass rate, etc.)

I've attached a draft MAP + Redwood evaluation template to save time. Camila and Diego are looped in to cover the technical plan.

Next steps: propose a 30–45 min technical kickoff this week (Camila + Diego + Sam + engineering lead). What time works for you?

Thanks,

Quick note from the engineering side — high level eval plan I propose: 

Objectives:
- Validate latency SLOs with representative workload
- Measure token/unit economics and cost per 1M tokens for chosen model family
- Validate relevance/quality against Helix's internal scorer

Phases (2–3 weeks):
1) Sanity & connectivity (2–3 days) — confirm S3 access, small smoke runs
2) Baseline run (4–6 days) — run with default model config to capture baseline latency/cost/quality
3) Optimization pass (4–6 days) — quantization, batching, and KV cache tuning; compare variants
4) Handoff & runbook (2–3 days) — produce performance report, recommended config, and rollout checklist

Data needs: 2–5k representative requests for the baseline (CSV/JSONL). If Helix provides streaming QPS profile, we can synthesize peak load tests.

I'll prepare a short test runner (Python + perf harness) and share a drive link before the kickoff.

— Diego
